John Corrill, a former leader and Church historian, gave the cost as “nearly forty thousand dollars” and stated that the Church was “thirteen or fourteen thousand dollars in debt” after the temple’s construction. “John Corrill, ‘Brief History,’ Manuscript, circa 1838–1839,” 33–34,josephsmithpapers.org. In 1837 Sidney Rigdon said that close to $13,000 in debt remained unpaid.
